requirement: Identify the governing public pair as NCT04906057/IRB 19-1003, The Therapeutic Effects of Forced Aerobic Exercise in Multiple Sclerosis: the seven-page protocol and separate two-page Statistical Analysis document both dated 15 July 2021; keep the reference analysis document annotation-only.

evidence.text: The protocol prints the exact title, NCT number 04906057, document date 07/15/2021 and principal investigator Susan Linder.
The separate analysis document repeats the exact title, NCT number and date and identifies IRB 19-1003.

requirement: Describe a prospective pilot randomized parallel-group study comparing forced aerobic exercise with voluntary aerobic exercise in people with multiple sclerosis.

evidence.text: The experimental overview describes a randomized pilot comparing FE and VE in people with MS.

requirement: Define the protocol population as adults aged 18 to 75 years with multiple sclerosis and an Expanded Disability Status Scale score from 2.0 through 6.5 who pass the ACSM exercise preparticipation health screen.

evidence.text: The overview and screening section state ages 18-75, MS, EDSS 2.0-6.5 and ACSM screening.

requirement: Randomize the 20 planned intervention participants 1:1 to FE or VE, with 10 planned per group, and stratify randomization by EDSS 2.0-4.0 versus 4.5-6.5.

evidence.text: The protocol plans n=10 in FE and n=10 in VE and stratifies randomization using the two EDSS ranges.

requirement: Before finalization, specify sequence generation, allocation concealment, block or other restrictions within EDSS strata, who enrolls and assigns participants, and how outcome-assessor masking is protected; do not invent these details.

evidence.text: The protocol states randomized assignment and EDSS stratification but supplies no operational sequence or concealment method.

requirement: Define both interventions as supervised semi-recumbent cycling twice weekly for 12 weeks in 45-minute sessions consisting of a 5-minute warm-up, 35-minute main set and 5-minute cool-down, with target heart rate at 60%-80% of age-predicted maximum.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the session frequency, duration, phases and target heart-rate intensity.

requirement: Distinguish FE from VE operationally: FE uses motor-assisted cadence targeting 80 RPM with five-RPM stepwise progression when initially intolerable, whereas VE uses an identical ergometer at self-selected cadence without motor assistance.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies the cadence and motor-assistance distinction and progression rule.

requirement: Define Aim 1 feasibility using percent of prescribed sessions attended, exercise time, time within the target heart-rate zone and absence of adverse events, with the protocol hypothesis of at least 90% compliance for frequency, time and intensity plus no worsening fatigue or sedentary activity.

evidence.text: Aim 1 and its hypothesis state the feasibility measures and the at-least-90% compliance criterion.

requirement: Operationalize the feasibility success rule across the several compliance components and the no-worsening fatigue, sedentary-activity and safety conditions, including whether all, any or a prespecified subset must meet threshold and whether the rule is assessed overall or by group.

evidence.text: The protocol states a compound feasibility hypothesis but does not define the logical success rule or denominator.

requirement: For Aim 2, retain change in biomechanical gait characteristics as the primary motor outcome and walking capacity, balance, manual dexterity and timed up-and-go as secondary motor outcomes, with baseline and post-intervention assessments.

evidence.text: Aim 2 and the outcome section identify the motor hierarchy and baseline/post-intervention measurements.

requirement: Before finalization, select and operationalize the gait-biomechanics variable or prespecified composite used as Aim 2 primary, including CAREN trial aggregation, side and limb rules, units and direction; do not treat the protocol's list of velocity, cadence, step, phase, support and joint-angle measures as one undefined endpoint.
acceptable_values: selected primary gait variable or composite

evidence.text: The protocol names gait biomechanics as primary and lists multiple spatiotemporal and kinematic measures without selecting one analysis variable.

requirement: For Aim 3, reconcile the non-motor endpoint hierarchy: PROMIS-29 is the protocol's primary quality-of-life outcome, while MSPT, CVLT and BVMT are called cognitive outcomes and partly called primary; define the primary variable, domain scoring, timepoint and direction for each without silently promoting all measures.

evidence.text: Aim 3 names PROMIS-29 as primary QOL and the cognitive instruments as primary outcomes for cognition but provides no single inferential hierarchy.

requirement: Define the randomized efficacy, intervention-exposed safety and feasibility-evaluable populations and treatment attribution, including participants who never start exercise, miss sessions, stop for cardiac symptoms, cross cadence targets, lack a post-intervention measure or withdraw.

evidence.text: The protocol defines randomization, attendance and stopping procedures but neither document defines analysis populations.

requirement: Define a randomized FE-versus-VE estimand for each selected motor and non-motor primary outcome, including population, baseline-to-post variable, treatment contrast, summary measure and strategies for exercise discontinuation, cadence intolerance, rescue or concomitant therapy, missing post-treatment outcome and death.

evidence.text: The protocol poses FE and VE hypotheses and allows intolerance/stopping but does not define estimands.

requirement: Use baseline-adjusted linear regression to estimate the randomized FE-versus-VE difference in each selected continuous post-treatment motor or non-motor outcome; treat paired within-group t tests only as supportive change analyses, not as the primary treatment comparison.

evidence.text: The plan calls for paired tests of within-participant change and separately calls for baseline-adjusted linear regressions comparing end-of-treatment outcomes between groups.

notes: The direct randomized contrast should be primary; the reference does not explicitly establish that hierarchy.

requirement: Summarize continuous demographics, participant characteristics and exercise parameters using mean and standard deviation or median and interquartile range as appropriate, and categorical variables using counts and percentages, by FE and VE group.

evidence.text: The first statistical-method paragraph gives these summaries and group stratification.

requirement: For longitudinal exercise parameters, fit a mixed-effects model with session and participant random effect; for cadence, include group and session-by-group interaction to estimate differential change, and prespecify session scale, covariance, degrees of freedom and nonlinear alternatives.

evidence.text: The plan specifies session-based mixed models with a participant random effect and group-by-session cadence analysis but omits implementation details.

requirement: Analyze Klotho as acute pre-to-post change at the first and last exercise sessions and long-term first-to-last-session change using a participant-level mixed model containing time dimensions and FE/VE group; analyze baseline-to-end NfL change supportively and define whether group interactions are estimated.

evidence.text: Aim 4 defines acute and long-term Klotho changes and baseline/end NfL.
The plan specifies paired tests and a Klotho mixed model with participant random effect and group indicator.

requirement: Specify outcome-specific missing-data handling for absent sessions, partial exercise recordings, unavailable heart-rate-zone time, missing baseline or post-treatment assessments, incomplete gait trials and missing biomarker draws; state the primary assumption and at least one sensitivity analysis for informative dropout or intolerance.

evidence.text: Repeated sessions, tolerance adjustments and multiple assessment modalities can generate partial data, but neither source defines missing-data rules.

requirement: Declare whether this pilot is estimation-focused or define confirmatory families and multiplicity control across feasibility components, multiple gait variables, PROMIS domains, cognitive tests, biomarkers, exercise parameters and repeated time contrasts; do not apply P<0.05 independently to every analysis.

evidence.text: The protocol defines four aims and many outcomes without an analysis hierarchy.
The reference applies P<0.05 without a multiplicity rule.

requirement: If formal tests are retained, clarify whether P<0.05 is two-sided, align alpha and confidence levels with the declared endpoint families and report adjusted or exploratory interpretation as applicable.

evidence.text: The plan says P<0.05 is significant but gives no sidedness, confidence level or multiplicity framework.

requirement: Use the prospective target of 20 randomized participants, 10 per group, with operational recruitment up to 24 for this pilot; do not substitute registry actual enrollment of 22 as the prospective target, and state that the source provides no formal power or precision calculation.

evidence.text: The overview plans 20 participants and 10 per group, while the recruitment section permits 24 recruited; no power assumptions are given.

requirement: Define exercise safety summaries using exposed-participant denominators and participant and event counts, including adverse events, cardiac distress, hemodynamic compromise, session stopping, cooling-vest use and rest breaks by group and intervention period; do not infer safety solely from zero events.

evidence.text: The protocol treats absence of adverse events as feasibility/safety and gives stopping, cooling and rest procedures but no statistical safety summaries.

requirement: Before finalization, confirm the during-recruitment prospective-governance chain and specify effect estimates with confidence intervals, diagnostic and fallback methods suitable for the small pilot, validated software and version, and reproducible model coding; present all unresolved choices as questions rather than invented facts.

evidence.text: The protocol is dated 15 July 2021, nine days after the registry's actual study-start date and well before primary completion.
The two-page plan lists tests and models but no confidence intervals, diagnostics, fallbacks, software or implementation detail.
